data.name: Sabrinia
data.gender_notes: Sabrinia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Roman mythology, Sabrina is a nymph associated with the River Severn in Wales. In Christian tradition, Sabrinia is derived from the Latin word 'saber' meaning 'sword'. Sabrinia may also be associated with Sabrina the saint, who is said to have been a Briton princess and a 7th-century martyr. The name Sabrinia carries the meaning “Sabre bearer” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Sabrinia usually hope their child will grow to embody sabre bearer and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: סבריניה
in_hebrew.meaning: השם סבריניה נגזר מהשם העברי סברינה, שפירושו גבירה או שפחה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם סבריניה קשור לשם העברי סברינה, שמקורו כנראה מהמילה 'סברה', שפירושו גבירה, או משורש עברי שפירושו שפחה. השם מופיע בשינויים שונים בכתבי הקודש ובמסורת היהודית, ויש לו קשרים עם המונחים 'גבירה' ו'אדונית'. השימוש בשם זה בקהילות נוצריות מעיד על הקשר בין השמות היהודיים והנוצריים.

in_greek.name: Σαβρίνια
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Σαβρίνια πιθανόν συνδέεται με τη λατινική λέξη 'Sabrina', που σημαίνει από το ποτάμι Severn στην Ουαλς
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σαβρίνια έχει πιθανές ρίζες από τη λατινική λέξη 'Sabrina', που αναφέρεται στο ποτάμι Severn στην Ουαλς. Αυτή η σύνδεση δείχνει την επιρροή της ρωμαϊκής και κελτικής κουλτούρας στην ονοματοδοσία. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοια ονόματα συνδέονται με έννοιες όπως 'από το ποτάμι' ή 'νερό', συμβολίζοντας ανανέωση και πνευματική κάθαρση.

in_latin.name: Sabrinia
in_latin.meaning: Nomen Sabrinia derivatum a Latina voce 'Sabrina', quae flumen Severn in Wallia significat
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Sabrinia originem ducit ex Latina voce 'Sabrina', quae nomen est fluminis Severn in Wallia. Hoc nomen in traditione christiana apparuisse videtur, ubi connotationes baptismales et renovationis spiritualis habet. Flumen Severn, quod vitam et fertilitatem suppeditat, inspirationem pro hoc nomine praebuisse videtur.

This name, associated with water and boundaries, symbolizes renewal and spiritual growth. Historically, it reflects the cultural exchange between Roman and Celtic traditions. In Christian contexts, Sabrinia may signify a connection to baptismal themes and spiritual rejuvenation. The name carries connotations of serenity, depth, and a connection to nature.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Sabrinia: Derived from the Sabine word "sabr" meaning "good, strong," or "worthy of reverence," Sabrinia symbolizes a woman who is both spiritually and physically robust, inspiring awe and respect through her unwavering faith and fortitude.

historical_references.reference: The legend of Sabrina, a British goddess of the river Severn, is told in Geoffrey of Monmouth's History of the Kings of Britain. Sabrina was a female deity associated with the river Severn in pre-Roman Britain. She was said to have drowned herself in the river when she could no longer bear the sorrow of seeing her lover, the god Maponos, killed in battle. In later Christian tradition, she was identified with the Virgin Mary and became the patroness of the river.

Saint Sabrina, also known as Sabra, was a virgin and martyr venerated in the Middle Ages, particularly in the towns of Sabratha and Thuburbo Majus in present-day Libya. According to legend, Sabrina was a Christian maiden who was martyred during the Roman persecutions of the late 3rd century AD. She was said to have been arrested, tortured, and beheaded, and her relics were later enshrined in a church dedicated to her.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern literature and media, the name Sabrinia is often associated with strong and independent women. It can be found in various fantasy novels, where Sabrinia is portrayed as a powerful sorceress, queen, or protector. The name also resonates with the trend of women's empowerment, as it evokes images of strength and resilience. Sabrinia is also featured in art and fan fiction on platforms such as Goodreads, Wattpad, and DeviantArt, where users can explore and share their creative interpretations of this name and its mythological associations.
